Definition: from G303 and G2334; to look again (i.e. attentively) at (literally or figuratively):--behold, consider.
BiblicalUsage: Twice the New Testament tells us to look carefully at something. Paul in Athens says he beheld the Athenians' devotions as he passed by, and Hebrews tells its readers to consider the end of their leaders' conversation. In both cases the word means a slow, attentive look, not a glance.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for looking closely holds no theology by itself; what it asks is simple, that we pay attention to what people worship and to how faithful lives end.
